code/rust/core_contracts/src/binding.rs: TypeBinding equality compares actual TypeId and intentionally ignores display names. Contract audit checks four associated type identities, requiring unit for Forbidden/NotApplicable, and implementation audit requires pointer identity with the contract descriptor. Public bridge trait may override its descriptor but pointer audit detects that. It explicitly does not validate registry authority/category/evidence/schema provenance; unused law comparator and numerous error variants do not imply such checks run. No operation is executed or behavioral law proven. Only manufactured Ok/Err test locally.
code/rust/core_contracts/src/core_contra: Offline stdin adapter reads at most64MiB+1, deserializes typed SourceBindingInput, runs the source-binding owner and outputs input SHA plus report with distinct success/incomplete/input/output exit codes. No path or provider access. Tests verify bounded reader consumption, exact/empty boundaries and duplicate top-level field refusal. The byte bound is concrete; parser allocation, static checker adequacy and report semantics depend on the called owner, not this wrapper. Generic reader helper's limit+1 assumes configured nonoverflowing limit, satisfied by constant.
code/rust/core_contracts/src/normal_form: Public serializable normal-form identity/classification/envelope DTOs with aliases and many defaults; purpose is arbitrary JSON, hashes/statuses are unchecked strings, authority is caller supplied. AuthorityTagged exposes outer authority without reconciling identity authority. No normalization function, equivalence relation, uniqueness proof or ZFNF rational checker occurs. Tests verify two wire shapes and serialization roundtrip, not claimed mathematical posture or semantic authority enforcement.
code/rust/core_contracts/src/runtime_sub: ReportManifest constructor refuses three supplied capability booleans (decide/mutate/execute) and sets EvidenceOnly; may_rank remains allowed. Public fields and Deserialize can bypass constructor, and timestamp/hash/source lists are unvalidated with no length correspondence or digest recomputation. dummy intentionally contains empty provenance. Tests cover constructor labels/refusals; no actual renderer side effects or read-only behavior are constrained by this metadata API.
code/rust/core_contracts/src/registry.rs: Reexports two structurally distinct corpus registries and explicitly disclaims runtime enforcement. Private CorpusPartition rejects repeated/intersecting caller u32 IDs and checks counts/addition; stores only cardinalities. Quadratic membership scans are finite but no resource ceiling. Its union==expected comparison is tautological because expected is assigned union; disjointness still follows from the explicit prior loops. Tests cover one disjoint and one overlap case. Does not inspect corpus contents or certify mathematics.
code/rust/core_contracts/src/mub_domain_: Fixed ten-row ownership and three-row conversion ledgers identify intended MUB, arithmetic, functional, runtime and certification owners. Validator checks surface uniqueness, canonical-role owner set, one Apache evidence record and existence of an F64Diagnostic forbidden-conversion string. It does not resolve modules/types, inspect conversions, ensure no contradictory additional conversion or execute MUB mathematics. Tests check fixed ledger consistency and physics-owner row. The ledger is architecture metadata, not evidence that exact/floating boundaries are enforced operationally.
code/rust/core_contracts/src/in_code_con: Private payload/phantom state enforces API progression through a caller-supplied FnOnce verifier to Verified then unconditional Admitted; no Deserialize or raw verified constructor. This proves only that the supplied callback returned Ok once, not its adequacy, purity or termination. T may have interior mutability and contract_id remains public, so post-verification truth/identity stability is not guaranteed. Predicate macros perform actual runtime boolean checks with typed early errors, not static proof or rollback of prior effects. Tests cover simple positive/negative payloads and division by zero; test-only integer division still has MIN/-1 panic and its quotient postcondition is not valid for all signed inputs.
code/rust/core_contracts/src/improvement: Namespace and concrete two-object key-order admission example: serializes reversed two-integer-field structs, compares bytes and three SHA computations and checked length equality. It establishes that fixture result only, not universal canonicalization or improvement correctness. Dependencies own encoding and DTOs; test runs that same sample. No automatic maintenance execution or authority promotion here.

Recursively sorts object keys, preserves array order/raw Unicode and restricts Number to i64/u64-representable integer values after serde_json::to_value. Generic Serialize input can lose type distinctions first: direct-source probe shows NaN and both infinities accepted as null with the same hash as None, despite documented float prohibition. Finite1.5 is refused. Parsed duplicate keys are already lost if supplied as Value; no input byte/depth limit. Tests cover nested order, Unicode, finite-float refusal and raw byte sensitivity, not nonfinite input. Encoding is its own integer JSON profile, not RFC8785/JCS.

Finding ID hashes detector version plus ordered path/content-hash/byte spans; candidate ID hashes ordered finding IDs and supplied baseline/replacement hash/path arrays. Body helper omits full bytes, authority, declared_write_surface and other policy fields by design. No validation of hash spelling, span grounding, equal vector lengths or actual bytes occurs. Span chain hashes fixed-width hex digests, avoiding concatenation ambiguity modulo hash assumptions. Tests cover order/version/path sensitivity; these are identifiers for declared material, not admission certificates.

Strict unknown-field DTOs contain no floating fields but public hash/schema/path/authority/always booleans remain unchecked. Defaults disable live provider and self-lane weight; terminal method always denies promotion. Span validator compares declared path/hash and end<=declared byte_len, not raw length/hash, so it requires a separately admitted source artifact. Base64 encoder is standard; exact decoder probe accepts misplaced/intermediate padding and nonzero padding bits (AA=A,AA==AAAA,AB==). Tests cover one raw-byte roundtrip and simple span bound, not malformed encoding or forged source metadata. Signed/frozen/independent labels and limits require host enforcement, absent here.
code/rust/core_contracts/src/nomos_urn.r: Concrete three-form ASCII URN grammar with digit-only three-component version and leading-zero refusal; version magnitude intentionally unbounded textual. Trims outer Unicode whitespace, so acceptance is normalized rather than byte-canonical. Rust-domain four-segment form wins over file marker. Public Deserialize/fields can create structures formatter accepts outside parser image; formatter explicitly renders an unrepresentable crate+file combination. Sample audit covers16positive/13negative vectors and debug-only roundtrip assertion, not entire identifier universe or source ownership. Nine local tests exercise grammar cases, not universal Rust/Python parity.
code/rust/core_contracts/src/nomos_urn_g: Test-only conformance adapter embeds a sibling fixture at compile time, validates schema/minimum28vectors/error-kind coverage, compares accepted parsed parts, refused error kinds, predicate agreement and accepted raw roundtrip against Python-owned recorded expectations. Tests offer bounded historical cross-language conformance, not independent grammar correctness or live Python execution. No fixture bytes reviewed or tests run in this step; include path and actual fixture availability must be resolved by build context. Shared capacity template has separate narrow meaning.
